advisor.summary: §179D grants an immediate deduction for energy-efficient commercial building property — interior lighting, HVAC and hot water, and envelope — certified against an ASHRAE 90.1 baseline, on a 2026 sliding scale that tops out at $5.94 per square foot when prevailing wage and apprenticeship standards are met. The controlling fact for 2026 planning is the OBBBA sunset: property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026 earns no deduction, so pipeline triage precedes any modeling. Government and tax-exempt owners cannot use the deduction but may allocate it to the building's designer, which makes §179D a recurring sweep for architecture and engineering clients with public work. Because the deduction reduces the property's basis, the benefit is acceleration against a 39-year schedule plus rate arbitrage — not new money — and the engine models it as a certified deduction amount against the owning entity's income.
mechanics: Qualifying property covers three systems only — interior lighting, HVAC and hot water, and building envelope — with the savings percentage set by energy modeling against the applicable ASHRAE 90.1 reference standard and certified by a qualified third party.

The 2026 deduction slides with modeled energy-cost savings from a $0.59-per-square-foot floor to a $1.19 cap, and multiplies five-fold — $2.97 up to $5.94 at the top — when prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance is documented from the start of construction; these are the 2026 inflation-adjusted amounts set by Rev. Proc. 2025-32.

P.L. 119-21 terminates §179D for property whose construction begins after June 30, 2026; projects that start construction by that date remain eligible when placed in service, so contemporaneous documentation of the start date belongs in the deliverable.

Buildings owned by governmental and tax-exempt entities generate a deduction the owner cannot use; §179D(d) lets the owner allocate it to the primary designer through a written allocation letter — a recurring benefit for design firms with schools and municipal work.
The deduction is claimed on Form 7205 and reduces the energy property's depreciable basis, so the modeled benefit is the certified amount taken now rather than ratably over the 39-year schedule.

requirements: A commercial building (or a residential building four stories or taller) with qualifying lighting, HVAC, or envelope work — and construction begun by June 30, 2026.
Third-party energy modeling and certification using IRS-approved software.
Prevailing wage and apprenticeship compliance tracked from the first day of construction if the multiplied rate is sought — it cannot be reconstructed after the fact.
For designer allocations, a signed allocation letter from the government or tax-exempt owner, retained in the file.
risks: The sunset dominates every other risk: a project that slips past the June 30, 2026 construction-start date gets nothing, so document 'physical work of a significant nature' contemporaneously — the begin-construction standard, not the placed-in-service date, controls.

A prevailing-wage or apprenticeship failure collapses the deduction to the base rate — roughly an 80% haircut — and the leading exam focus is certification quality and wage documentation, not any single litigated case.
The deduction reduces basis: later depreciation shrinks and gain on sale grows, so the benefit is timing plus rate arbitrage and should be presented as exactly that.
The indexed per-square-foot figures change annually; quoting last year's numbers misstates the benefit.
Allocation letters that are unsigned, late, or vague about the 'primary designer' fail on exam — paper them at project close-out, not at return time.
stateNotes: Conformity: states that start from federal taxable income or AGI generally conform to §179D automatically; verify any decoupled or selective-conformity state in the client’s footprint before combining benefits.
Missouri conforms through its federal starting point (RSMo §143.091, §143.121), so the federal deduction flows into the Missouri computation with no separate addback.

PTET interaction: for a pass-through owner, the §179D deduction shrinks the entity income a PTET election is computed on; designer allocations to a firm with a PTET election follow the same sequencing.
reviewChecklist: Construction-start date documented and safely before July 1, 2026.
Certification package complete: qualified certifier, approved software, ASHRAE baseline identified, savings percentage stated.
Wage-and-apprenticeship records support the multiplied rate where claimed.
Designer allocation letter signed by the owner and naming the primary designer, where applicable.
Basis reduction posted to the fixed-asset records, with the modeled amount tied to the certification.

client.teaser: Energy-smart building work earns a sizable deduction — but only for projects that start soon.
client.headline: A big deduction for efficient buildings — and a firm deadline
plainEnglish: When you build or upgrade a commercial building with efficient lighting, heating and cooling, or a better shell, the tax law rewards you. Instead of spreading those costs over 39 years, you deduct a set amount per square foot right away. On a large building, that adds up fast.

There is a catch. Congress ended this break for projects that begin construction after June 30, 2026. Work that starts before then stays eligible. Right now, the calendar matters more than anything else.

The deduction grows with the building's certified energy savings. It grows five times larger when the crews are paid at certain wage standards. An independent engineer certifies the savings, and that certificate is your proof.
client.analogy: It is like a rebate program in its final season — the reward is real, but the entry window closes on June 30, 2026.
benefits: A deduction of up to several dollars per square foot, taken right away
Five times larger when wage standards are met on the job
Design firms can receive the deduction on government projects
Works for upgrades to existing buildings, not just new construction
steps: WE check your project dates against the June 30, 2026 start deadline — first.
WE arrange the certified energy modeling and review the results.
WE claim the deduction on the right IRS form and update your building records.
YOU keep the construction contracts and payroll records that prove dates and wages.
clientCommitments: Start qualifying construction before the deadline and keep proof of the start date
Have your contractor track wage and apprentice records from day one if the larger rate is the goal

annualMaintenance: Sweep the project pipeline each year for buildings placed in service with certification still open
For design-firm clients, collect allocation letters on eligible public projects as they close out
deliverables: Deadline-triage memo mapping every project against the construction-start cutoff
Certification package (energy model, certifier statement, wage documentation)
